files.name: project-summary-sidecar.json
files.title: Inventory Management — Project Summary
files.description: Inventory Management is a Klinswork Project concerned with reliable knowledge and operational control of inventory. Its principal known System is Inventory 3.0. The Project is defined independently of its current name, hierarchy, repository location, application, datastore, Resource set, deployment, or operational environment. The current exemplar now includes a Project Identity record, local README, human-readable Project Summary, and this structured companion sidecar; System-local documentation, discovery testing, Viewer testing, Resource reconciliation, and final reusable Project Definition extraction remain.

files.name: system-summary-sidecar.json
files.title: Inventory 3.0 — System Summary
files.description: Inventory 3.0 is the principal known System serving the Inventory Management Project. Historical design records describe a mobile-friendly Google Apps Script web application using Google Sheets, event-based inventory changes, current-inventory state, product/location/SDS reference data, validation, history, and later administration/reporting. Historical July 2026 records show the System was actually built and expanded. This documentation step intentionally does not create system-identity.json or assign a SYS-###, and it does not treat historical plans as proof of current live behavior.

files.name: nmbhi-first-supervisor-profile-sidecar-3.0-draft.json
files.title: Profile of My First Supervisor at NMBHI
files.description: The document argues that the supervisor’s success did not rest on charisma or unusually motivated employees. It came from a connected operating system. Workers had known schedules, shared training, clear authority, communication rules, standardized supplies, predictable inspections, audited records, immediate feedback, and continuous follow-up. These practices reduced uncertainty, made standards visible, produced relatively uniform results from different workers, and allowed workplace harmony to emerge from operational clarity.
